clue.text: Understood this Roman style of architecture

parts.note: 'got it' means understood it, so understood gives got
hic is the Latin, so Roman, word for this

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a building's look is classical Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' points to the Latin word for 'this'; the surface suggests a Roman building, which the answer is not.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed-arch medieval building manner of Europe's cathedrals is called by this name.

clue.text: Like bone meal found in a lot of slow cooking

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other, so the light meal sits within the cooked letters
cooking works the letters over into a new mixture, signalling a rearrangement
a lot of a word, but not all of it, so the final letter of slow is dropped

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: Bone meal turns up in a big pot of slow-cooked food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter; 'cooking' rearranges what is left; 'found in' puts the meal inside. 'Bone meal' looks like one phrase, but 'Like bone' is the definition and 'meal' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the technical medical term for something relating to or made of skeleton tissue.

clue.text: Hotel on a river — stay with family

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Ouse is a river in England (several share the name)
to stay something is to hold it, as in hold back

explanation.surface: Lodging in a riverside hotel with relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Those living together under one roof form a domestic unit, a family in the wide sense.

clue.text: Trade article forces ministry to follow order in City

indicators.note: the pair of abbreviations goes in the word for a city, splitting it

parts.note: taken as written, the word city

indicators.note: the ministry comes after the order, so these words fix the order of the two pieces

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
MOD is the Ministry of Defence, the ministry over the armed forces

explanation.surface: A traded item makes the armed forces' department fall into line in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the two abbreviations inside the city word, after its first letter; 'to follow' fixes the ministry after the honour. 'forces' looks like a verb but is part of the ministry's description.
explanation.definitionFit: An item bought and sold, such as grain or oil, is a raw good of trade.

clue.text: This shot through with cinnamon and raisins?

definitions.text: This shot through with cinnamon and raisins?

parts.words: This shot through with cinnamon and raisins?
parts.note: reads like something streaked with spice, but describes a folded pastry case holding spiced fruit filling

explanation.surface: Something laced with spice and dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded-over pastry filled with fruit, often apple spiced with cinnamon, is named this way.

clue.text: Sailor doubled energy with fish sauce

indicators.note: doubled means the word for sailor appears twice in a row

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A seaman, twice as lively, pairs his fish with a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayonnaise-based relish with capers served with fried fish is spelt in the French way here.

clue.text: Tree line and delta unseen

parts.note: a row is a line of things side by side

indicators.note: unseen means that letter is made to vanish from the word and

parts.note: D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A row of trees by a river delta that cannot be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, with red berries, is a familiar tree of this name.

clue.text: No secret hole on green

parts.note: O is shaped like a hole
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golf hole on the putting green is no secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' and 'hole' suggest golf; vert is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly, not hidden, is plain for all to see.

clue.text: Hugely popular?

parts.note: reads as very much liked, but asks for a word meaning huge, like a hit that was very big

explanation.surface: A massive hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossal success is often described with this adjective meaning vast in size.

clue.text: On road, percussionist shuns lead guitarist

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road

indicators.note: shuns its lead means the drummer word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a drummer plays percussion

explanation.surface: Out on tour, the drummer avoids the band's lead guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Strummer was guitarist and singer of the Clash; the surface sets up a band on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Strummer, of the punk band the Clash, played rhythm guitar, so he is a famous example.

clue.text: Guitarist's little tutor

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a don is a university tutor

explanation.surface: A small teaching book by a guitar player.
explanation.walkthrough: Bert Weedon was a British guitarist whose 'Play in a Day' tutor book taught a generation, which the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Bert Weedon was a British guitar player famed for his teaching manual.

clue.text: 50 are attending party in American city

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the party word comes alongside, after the rest

parts.note: L is 50 in Roman numerals
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Fifty guests go to a party in a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a city in Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Never in a million years, for example

definitions.text: Never in a million years, for example

parts.words: Never in a million years, for example
parts.note: a phrase like 'never in a million years' is an emphatic way of saying on no occasion whatever

explanation.surface: An emphatic refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something will happen on no occasion ever is the plain meaning of this emphatic idiom.

clue.text: Magic quarter of 14

indicators.note: a quarter of the twelve-letter answer at 14 is its opening three letters

parts.note: 14 points to the twelve-letter answer at 14-across, the Latin legal phrase

explanation.surface: A bit of conjuring drawn from another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 refers to the answer at 14-across, twelve letters long, so a quarter is three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, also spelt obeah, is a form of folk sorcery from the Caribbean.

clue.text: Working it out, McBride gives an opinion — just?

indicators.note: working the letters over means rearranging them

explanation.surface: McBride figures it out and pronounces a view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges IT OUT and MCBRIDE. The definition plays on 'just': a passing remark by a judge, so a justice, and only an opinion, not binding.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a judge's incidental remark, not binding as precedent, carries this Latin name.

clue.text: Do not read about air-freshener

indicators.note: about here means turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction not to read up on room sprays.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray or stick that masks body or room odours freshens the air.

clue.text: Scowled at, breaks into this!

indicators.note: breaks means the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone glared at bursts into nervous perspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges SCOWLED AT; the whole clue also says what a person glared at might break into.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear or anxiety brings on clammy perspiration, which people say they break into.

clue.text: Slug in news report

parts.note: a slug is a bullet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slug features in a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: A short official news broadcast or statement is called this.

clue.text: Conservative should say 'no problem with religious instruction'

indicators.note: problem marks the letters before it as a puzzle to be sorted out

explanation.surface: A Tory claims faith teaching is no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges C with SHOULD SAY NO; the quotation marks make 'no problem' look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Children learn religion at church classes held on the sabbath.

clue.text: Like hard wood

parts.note: as means like
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something resembling solid timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'hard wood', but 'hard' gives H and 'wood' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tough timber used for tool handles, so it names a wood.

clue.text: Claim to know nurse

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or know
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Asserting acquaintance with a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or maintain a point is to argue for it.

clue.text: Powerful banker's euro-investment sequence

indicators.note: investment here means being put inside, enclosed by the banker

parts.note: the Gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for powerful Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A mighty financier's euro deal follows a pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is used in its old sense of enclosing: E goes inside GNOME.
explanation.definitionFit: The full DNA sequence of an organism is its complete set of genes.

clue.text: Tie's good, shown in amusing light for the camera

indicators.note: shown in means displayed inside the funny word

parts.note: fun means amusing
to lash is to tie

explanation.surface: A man shows off a comic tie for the photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer's lamp gives a burst of light to illuminate the subject.

clue.text: No buyer attracted to this antique coin?

definitions.text: No buyer attracted to this antique coin?

parts.words: No buyer attracted to this antique coin?
parts.note: playfully read as '...' (sold to nobody), so an old coin that drew zero bidders

explanation.surface: An old coin that failed to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldo was an old Italian coin; split as SOLD plus O (nothing), it is a sale to no one.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldo was a small coin of old Italy, from Latin solidus.

clue.text: One excused master class

indicators.note: excused means let off, so the one is sent out of the word

parts.note: a genius is a master of an art
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One pupil is let off the master's lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master class' looks like one item; 'master' gives GENIUS and 'class' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a rank of classification above species is a group of related kinds.

clue.text: Secretive person in the pink

definitions.meaning: a closed, uncommunicative person is likened to a shellfish that stays shut
a pale greyish-pink shade is named after the shellfish

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish that clams up suggests the reticent; its colour is a pinkish white.

clue.text: Fur, new, taken dishonestly

parts.note: a stole is a fur wrap

explanation.surface: A new fur coat was nicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Property obtained by theft has been pinched.

clue.text: Always pinching a penny at the expense of stateswoman

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between, so the word for always holds the other letters

parts.note: ever means always
'on' as in 'the drinks are on me'

explanation.surface: Constantly saving a penny at the cost of a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' puts A and P inside EVER; Eva Perón was the wife of Argentina's president.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine first lady was a powerful political figure in her own right.

clue.text: Red-nosed drunk given support

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tippler with a red nose gets backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate or product that is backed publicly has been approved.

clue.text: Songbird was first to be handled with respect

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: A singing bird that came first deserves careful treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handled' puns on 'handle', slang for a title: a lord is addressed respectfully by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a rank such as lord or lady bears an honorific handle.
